key_insight: Trivalent planar qubit architectures can support scalable lattice surgery for surface-code logical entanglement with lower overhead than conventional four-valent schemes.
engineering_relevance: This reduces qubit and gate resources needed for fault-tolerant quantum processors, making nearest-neighbor hardware layouts more practical for scalable quantum computing.
method: Develop scalable lattice-surgery circuit constructions tailored to degree-3 planar connectivity.
Compare resource scaling against the four-valent measurement scheme.
Benchmark logical fidelity with experimentally realistic fluxonium-based simulations.
evidence_signal: Simulations indicate up to about 25% improvement in logical fidelity at distance three for the trivalent protocol.
watch_item: The reported benefit is demonstrated in realistic simulations and at small code distance, so hardware noise, routing constraints, and scaling behavior still need experimental validation.
paper_title: Towards logical entanglement creation in trivalent planar architectures
